title: Optimize Guardrails — Metrics + Cardinality Review (Telemetry Design Notes)
body:
Context
- We’re adding quality guardrails gating for Optimize apply. We need telemetry that:
  (a) powers dashboards/alerts for gating health
  (b) lets us correlate config-change → eval outcome → post-change customer signals
  (c) stays within metric cardinality limits (Prometheus + our internal M3 ingestion)
  (d) is safe: no prompt text, no raw model outputs, minimal tenant-identifying labels

Attendees
- Logan Wright (Telemetry/datasets)
- Nadia Rahman (Cost attribution)
- Caleb Johnson (Tracing/metrics ingestion)
- Allison Grant (Observability standards)
- Sean Gallagher + Rafael Mendes (SRE)
- Ethan Park + Jordan Lee (Control plane/policy engine)
- Selene Huang (Guardrails lead)

Scope of this review
- Metric names + which are counters vs histograms/gauges
- Label set + which labels are allowed at metric time-series level
- What must be an audit event only (structured log) vs a metric
- Sampling: what is 100% vs what is sampled, and at which point (emitter vs collector)

Terminology
- “Gating run”: evaluation job executed for an Optimize apply attempt (may be cached).
- “Suite”: eval harness suite selection (e.g., quantization_min, tool_calling_sentinel).
- “Decision”: pass/fail/blocked/timeout/override_applied/etc.

1) Proposed metric set (v0)

1.1 Topline outcomes (dashboards)
A) optimize_guardrails_apply_attempts_total (counter)
- Meaning: count of apply attempts that reached guardrails decisioning.
- Required labels:
  - decision = {pass, fail, timeout, error, blocked_runner_down, blocked_policy, override_applied, override_requested}
  - enforcement_mode = {observe_only, soft_block, hard_block}
  - optimization_type = {quantization, batching, caching, routing}
  - tier = {hosted, dedicated, private} (NOTE: keep small, do not add per-tenant)
  - env = {prod, staging}
- Optional labels (tentative, see cardinality notes):
  - workload_tag = {chat, embeddings, rerank, tool_calling, structured_output, mixed} (must come from a small controlled set)

B) optimize_guardrails_eval_jobs_total (counter)
- Meaning: jobs created in eval runner.
- Labels:
  - status = {enqueued, started, succeeded, failed, timed_out, canceled}
  - suite_group = {quantization, batching, caching, routing, general} (suite_group only; not suite_id)
  - env

C) optimize_guardrails_eval_job_latency_ms (histogram)
- Meaning: end-to-end job latency (enqueue → terminal state). Used for SLO and backlog diagnosis.
- Labels:
  - status = {succeeded, failed, timed_out}
  - suite_group
  - env

D) optimize_guardrails_eval_cache_hits_total (counter)
- Meaning: cache effectiveness for gating runs.
- Labels:
  - cache_result = {hit, miss, bypass}
  - suite_group
  - env

1.2 Failure reason breakdown
We need failure reasons, but must avoid high-cardinality “reason strings” as labels.

Proposal:
- optimize_guardrails_apply_failures_total (counter)
  - Labels:
    - failure_class = {metric_regression, min_samples_not_met, ci_too_wide, eval_runner_error, policy_eval_error, artifacts_missing, schema_validation}
    - optimization_type
    - enforcement_mode
    - env

Do NOT include:
- metric_name as a label at this level (too many + changes over time)
- suite_id as a label (unbounded over time)

Instead, include detailed breakdown in structured audit event (see section 3).

1.3 Runner health / backlog
- optimize_guardrails_eval_queue_depth (gauge)
  - Labels: queue = {default, high_pri} (max 2), env
- optimize_guardrails_eval_workers_active (gauge)
  - Labels: worker_pool = {default}, env

2) Label policy (cardinality constraints)

Hard rules (metrics)
- No tenant_id / org_id as a metric label.
- No route_id / endpoint path as a metric label.
- No model_id / model_version as a metric label.
- No prompt_set_id / prompt_set_revision as a metric label.
- No suite_id as a metric label.
- No freeform text labels.

Rationale
- All of the above explode time series in production (tenant count + model versions + per-route diversity).
- We still need these dimensions for debugging; they belong in audit logs and traces.

Controlled enums allowed as labels (metrics)
- env, tier, optimization_type, enforcement_mode, decision
- suite_group (small set)
- status (small set)
- failure_class (small set)
- region (tentative). If we add region, must be normalized to our canonical small list (e.g., {us-east1, us-west1, eu-west1}) and only for runner metrics; do not add to apply outcomes unless SRE insists.

Open question: workload_tag
- Pros: helpful to see if tool-calling / structured-output is driving failures.
- Cons: will drift and become quasi-freeform unless controlled.
- Decision: allow workload_tag ONLY if it is a validated enum from the policy schema (rejected if unknown). No raw “customer-provided” tags.

3) Structured events (audit logs) vs metrics

Anything needing high-cardinality dimensions moves to events.

3.1 Required audit event: OptimizeConfigChange (already in spec)
- Event name (per Security spec): OptimizeConfigChange
- Must include (structured fields, not metric labels):
  - actor_id (redacted / internal ID)
  - org_id (internal)
  - project_id / workspace_id (if applicable)
  - model_family, model_id, model_version
  - optimization_type
  - config_delta_summary (bounded size)
  - guardrails:
    - enforcement_mode
    - decision
    - override_flag + override_justification (if any)
    - gating_run_id
    - suite_ids (array) + suite_version
    - prompt_set_id + prompt_set_revision
    - per_metric_results: metric_name, baseline, candidate, delta, threshold, pass/fail, ci_low/high, n_samples
- NOTE: This doc is not redefining the Security event schema; we’re calling out that per-metric details should be event-only.

3.2 New event (proposed): GuardrailsGatingRunSummary
- Motivation: OptimizeConfigChange is “apply-centric.” We also want runner-centric runs (replays, nightly sentinels, backfills).
- Fields:
  - gating_run_id, created_at, terminal_status, runtime_ms
  - suite_ids (array) + suite_group
  - model_id, model_version, prompt_set_revision
  - cache_key_hash (NOT raw key; hash only)
  - decision + failure_class (if fail)
- Storage/retention: follow eval artifacts retention (see PR/issue ENG-??; not final here).

4) Tracing

We will rely on traces for per-request debugging (low sampling).

Trace spans (OpenTelemetry)
- optimize.apply (root)
  - attributes (OK in traces even if high-cardinality): org_id, apply_id, optimization_type, enforcement_mode
  - child: guardrails.policy_eval
  - child: guardrails.eval_runner.enqueue
  - child: guardrails.eval_runner.poll

Important: traces must not include prompt text or model outputs.
- If we need evidence of “format drift,” capture a bounded hash of output structure (e.g., json_schema_validation_result + error_code), not raw content.

Sampling (traces)
- prod: 0.1% baseline for optimize.apply traces
- bump to 1% for hard-block stage for first 2 weeks (time-bound) IF ingestion budget allows
- always sample error traces (tail-based) where decision in {error, timeout} up to a cap

5) Sampling strategy (metrics + events)

Metrics
- Counters/histograms listed above should be 100% emitted. They are low-cardinality by design.

Audit events
- OptimizeConfigChange: 100% (compliance + customer ask; see SUP-18544 reference in CS notes)
- GuardrailsGatingRunSummary: 100% in staging; in prod, 100% for runs tied to an apply attempt; optionally sample for “background” runs (nightly sentinels/backfills) if volume spikes.

Per-prompt eval results
- DO NOT emit per-prompt metrics.
- Keep per-prompt details only in eval artifact store (object store / DB) with retention.
- If we must have “example failures,” store up to K exemplars per suite with aggressive redaction + hashing (Applied ML to define; likely separate doc).

6) Cardinality risk checklist (things we almost did but should not)
- Label by model_version: rejected (model versions roll frequently; tons of series)
- Label by prompt_set_revision: rejected (frequent + combinatorial)
- Label by metric_name: rejected (taxonomy evolves; also breaks dashboards)
- Label by suite_id: rejected (suite_id count grows; merges/splits over time)
- Label by route_id: rejected (customer-defined, huge)
- Label by org_id: rejected (huge + sensitive)

7) Naming conventions
- Metrics follow: optimize_guardrails_<noun>_<unit> (snake_case)
- Suffixes:
  - *_total for counters
  - *_ms for latency
- Label keys: decision, status, env, tier, enforcement_mode, optimization_type, suite_group, failure_class
- Avoid “result” vs “status” confusion:
  - status = lifecycle of job (enqueued/started/succeeded/failed)
  - decision = guardrails output used by apply (pass/fail/timeout/blocked/etc.)

8) Dashboards/alerts implications (SRE)
- Primary SRE panels (match observability-pack/pr_441):
  - Apply decision breakdown (% pass/% fail/% timeout)
  - Eval job latency p50/p95 by suite_group
  - Queue depth
  - Cache hit rate
  - Error budget burn for timeouts/errors

Alert candidates
- High timeout rate: optimize_guardrails_apply_attempts_total{decision="timeout"} / total > X% over 10m
- Runner failures: optimize_guardrails_eval_jobs_total{status="failed"} increase > threshold
- Queue depth sustained > N for M minutes

NOTE: Alerts should be tier-aware only at the dashboard-level (filter by tier), not via separate alert rules per-tenant.

9) Action items / decisions
- [Decision] No high-cardinality labels in metrics (org_id, model_version, suite_id, metric_name, prompt_set_revision).
- [Decision] failure_class is the only “reason” label permitted for now.
- [AI-1] (Logan) Update telemetry emitter spec in ENG-3918 with final metric list + allowed labels. Due 2025-02-07.
- [AI-2] (Caleb) Confirm collector-side constraints: max label cardinality per metric + eviction behavior. Add a short note here once confirmed. Due 2025-02-05.
- [AI-3] (Allison) Review naming conventions for consistency with company standards + reserve prefixes. Due 2025-02-06.
- [AI-4] (Sean/Rafael) Provide initial alert thresholds for timeout/error rates consistent with rollout stages (observe-only → soft-block → hard-block). Due 2025-02-10.
- [AI-5] (Ethan/Jordan) Ensure audit event includes gating_run_id + suite_ids + prompt_set_revision for customer audit requirements (but keep metrics low-card). Due 2025-02-07.

Open questions
- Do we need region on apply outcome metrics? SRE wants it for “is this one region’s runner broken.” Telemetry wants to keep it runner-only. Proposed compromise: add region ONLY on eval job metrics; correlate via traces/events when needed.
- How to represent “manual approval” vs “override”? Product wording is still in flux. Telemetry can support both decisions, but needs final enum values before GA.
- Retention/volume: If we emit GuardrailsGatingRunSummary for every background run, do we exceed log budget? To revisit after pilot volume numbers.

Appendix: Controlled enums (draft)
- decision: pass | fail | timeout | error | blocked_runner_down | blocked_policy | override_applied | override_requested
- enforcement_mode: observe_only | soft_block | hard_block
- optimization_type: quantization | batching | caching | routing
- suite_group: quantization | batching | caching | routing | general
- failure_class: metric_regression | min_samples_not_met | ci_too_wide | eval_runner_error | policy_eval_error | artifacts_missing | schema_validation
